title: Delta Cohort Explorer and Automated Investigation for Benchmark Regressions
creator: Arielle Porter
description: Problem: Our current benchmark result store and comparison UI surface the final delta numbers, but when p95 or tokens/sec regress, it takes manual investigation across runs to determine whether regressions are noise, a specific workload cohort, or caused by infra/model changes. This ticket designs and builds a 'Delta Cohort Explorer' plus an automated investigation pipeline that generates reproducible evidence bundles for triage.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Result store supports cohort metadata and fast delta queries across model/hardware/payload tags
A2: UI component shows cohorted heatmap, sparkline for p50/p95/tokens_per_sec and allows pinning two cohorts for side-by-side diff
A3: Auto-investigation job runs on anomaly detection and produces an evidence bundle (replay traces, kernel selection, kv-cache hit rates, failure traces) linked to the UI
A4: Triage workflow creates a Linear sub-issue automatically with prefilled hypothesis and suggested next steps when anomaly score > threshold
A5: End-to-end latency for generating evidence bundle <= 15 minutes for a typical regression signal
comments: 2026-02-20 Miguel Santos: Kickoff meeting notes - scoped MVP to p95 and tokens/sec, cohort dimensions = [model_variant, instance_type, sequence_profile, prompt_template]. Agreed to reuse existing benchmark blob layout but add a lightweight metadata index.
2026-02-24 Infra review (L. Chen): Prefers Parquet artifact store in S3 and Postgres for metadata indexes. Raised cost concern for frequent scans; suggested partitioning by week + model_id.

2026-03-01 Design feedback (R. Vega): UX should prioritize quick triage actions: 'Create Incident', 'Open Replay', 'Pin Comparison', and an exportable evidence bundle. Provide example mockups in Figma (link in links).
2026-03-05 Engineering sync: Chose anomaly detector v2 (EWMA + seasonal decomposition) rather than ML classifier for MVP due to explainability. Will add ML scorer in follow-up.

2026-03-10 Miguel Santos: Implemented storage schema migration patch and ingestion adapter. Running smoke ingest on a 30-day partition. Observed 12% storage overhead vs baseline because of per-request fingerprints.

2026-03-12 QA notes (N. Patel): First auto-investigation runs produced reproducible evidence bundles for 3/4 seeded regressions. One failure was due to missing kernel logs; added a missing-sidecar task to capture kernel selection metadata.
implementation_notes: Storage: store raw run blobs in S3 (gzipped protobuf) and write a compact row to Postgres per run with precomputed aggregates and a JSONB 'cohort_keys' field for quick filtering (MVP). Partition postgres by model_id + week.
Indexing: generate a deterministic fingerprint for each run using (model_variant, instance_type, seq_profile_hash, prompt_template_hash, timestamp_bucket). Use fingerprint to group runs into cohorts.

Delta algorithm: compute two-sided bootstrap CI around p95 and tokens/sec; flag candidate regressions when lower bound of new run p95 > upper bound of baseline p95 by configured delta_percentage or when tokens/sec drops by > X% with p < 0.01.

Auto-investigation pipeline: on anomaly -> enqueue job that replays representative traces against selected baseline and current model, collects kernel selection logs, KV cache hit rates, batch sizes, env metadata, and stores a signed evidence bundle in S3 and links it in the UI.

UI: add a cohort explorer with hierarchical filters (model -> hardware -> prompt family -> traffic bucket), heatmap tiles for p95/tokens/sec, and a 'Compare' mode that shows side-by-side per-step breakdown and diff waterfall.

Triage integration: when anomaly score > 0.8, create Linear sub-issue with prefilled title 'Regression candidate: <model> <date>' and attach evidence bundle URL, suggested rollbacks, and labels (regression, production-impact).
Observability hooks: instrument runtime to emit kernel selection, quantization profile, batch_size, and kv_cache_hit_rate events keyed by run_id. These are required by the auto-investigation job.
Privacy/compliance: evidence bundle must redact user prompt text unless flagged by the test harness (use synthetic prompts in system-critical tests).
decisions: D1: Use deterministic cohort fingerprints instead of dynamic clustering for MVP to keep grouping reproducible across runs.
D2: Use explainable statistical tests for alerting initially (bootstrap/ewma) and reserve ML models for second-stage scoring.
D3: Evidence bundles will be immutable, versioned artifacts stored in S3 with signed metadata to make triage audit-friendly.
D4: UI will not attempt automated rollback; it will provide recommended actions only to force human-in-the-loop approval.
D5: Partitioning strategy chosen to limit Postgres scan costs: weekly partitions + model_id prefix.
